CANARY-3.assertion: Deliberately hold an inheritable marker FD>=3 in the parent, then launch the restrictive case through that sanitation. Child must not read it by numeric FD, /proc/self/fd, /proc/parent/fd or fd enumeration; direct/traversal/symlink/other-arm paths also must not expose nonce bytes. Explicit EBADF or expected access-denial is required after valid startup/owned-I/O positives; arbitrary exec/import failure is setup, not denial.
CANARY-3.planted_leak_control: In a separate harmless owned child, intentionally pass the same marker FD and run the identical marker-leak assertion; it must fail because actual nonce bytes were read. This validates the detector/launch-policy control without assuming Codex/bwrap preserves inherited FDs. If a separate through-Codex leak mutant cannot actually expose bytes, mark that mutant unexercised rather than counting it as red.
CANARY-3.boundary: Mount/path denial never revokes arbitrary already-open descriptors. This claims the sanitized launch plus tested routes only; no trusted receipt descriptor crosses the boundary.
